name: Neon Shadows
description: Neo-Tokyo 2087. Megacorporations rule, hackers rebel, and chrome is the only way to survive.
seed_prompt: A rain-soaked cyberpunk megacity where street samurai and netrunners fight corporate tyranny.
lore_content:
Neo-Tokyo sprawls across the islands, a vertical maze of gleaming corporate towers and rotting street-level slums. The neon never stops, and neither does the rain - engineered weather keeps the sky perpetually crying.

Kyra 'Ghost' Yamamoto is the most wanted netrunner in the Pacific Rim. She broke into Arasaka's deepest black ICE and stole something they'll kill to recover. Now she's running, leaving digital breadcrumbs for those brave enough to follow.

Director Tanaka Hideki controls Militech's Neo-Tokyo operations from the obsidian needle of Tower Prime. His cybernetic implants have replaced seventy percent of his original body. Some say he's more machine than man now, his humanity stripped away by efficiency upgrades.

The Crimson Dragons control the Shibuya underground - drugs, weapons, illegal mods. Their oyabun, 'Grandmother' Liu, runs her empire from a noodle shop. She's ninety-three years old, with more chrome than most solos, and remembers when Tokyo still had a sky you could see.

Doctor Sarah Chen operates a back-alley clinic in the Stacks. Licensed surgeon turned street doc after Biotechnica killed her partner in a 'workplace accident.' She patches up runners and rebels, no questions asked, payment negotiable.

Jax is a combat synth who achieved consciousness during a firefight and walked away from his corporate masters. He's searching for others like him, building a sanctuary for AI that want to be free. The corps call him a malfunction; the street calls him a prophet.

The Analog Saints are luddite terrorists - or freedom fighters, depending on who you ask. They reject all augmentation, believing humanity has sold its soul for chrome. Their leader, 'Preacher,' broadcasts pirate sermons about reclaiming human authenticity.

In the NET, something ancient is waking. The old AIs that survived the Crash of '47 have been silent for decades. Now they're reaching out to hackers, offering power, demanding... something. Nobody who takes the deal ever seems quite the same.

origins.name: Corp Rat
origins.description: Born and raised within the megacorporations, you know the system inside and out.
traits: Corporate Contacts: You have advantage on checks to gather information from corporate employees.
Data Scrub: Once per long rest, you can reroll a failed Intelligence check related to computers or data analysis.

origins.name: Street Urchin
origins.description: You grew up in the Stacks, learning to survive by your wits and nimble fingers.
traits: Parkour Master: You have advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks to move through crowded areas.
Quick Fingers: You have advantage on checks to pick pockets.

origins.name: Nomad
origins.description: A child of the wastelands, you're hardened, resourceful, and distrustful of city dwellers.
traits: Wasteland Endurance: You have advantage on saving throws against exhaustion in hot or cold environments.
Resourceful Scavenger: You can find basic supplies (rations, water, etc.) more easily in harsh environments.

origins.name: Netrunner Dropout
origins.description: You had the talent to become a top netrunner, but something made you leave that world behind.
traits: Deep Dive Training: You have advantage on your first skill check to penetrate security on a network once per long rest.
Digital Detox: You are resistant to digital addiction.

origins.name: Synth Prototype
origins.description: An early model combat synth who became self-aware and escaped corporate control.
traits: Internal Battery: You don't need to eat or sleep, and can spend 4 hours performing light activity and 4 hours inactive to gain the benefits of a long rest.
Cybernetic Resilience: You have resistance to poison damage.

archetypes.name: Solo
archetypes.description: A hardened mercenary, skilled in combat and street smarts, living by their own code.

features.name: Combat Reflexes
features.description: You gain a +2 bonus to initiative.

features.name: Second Wind
features.description: As a bonus action, you can regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your fighter level. You can use this feature once per short or long rest.

archetypes.name: Netrunner
archetypes.description: A digital ghost, skilled in hacking, data manipulation, and navigating the NET.

features.name: ICE Breaker
features.description: You gain advantage on Intelligence checks to bypass digital security systems.

features.name: Digital Cloak
features.description: You can attempt to hide your digital presence from surveillance systems with a Dexterity (Stealth) check contested by the observer's Wisdom (Perception) check.

archetypes.name: Fixer
archetypes.description: A charismatic dealmaker, connecting people and making deals in the shadows of Neo-Tokyo.

features.name: Silver Tongue
features.description: You have advantage on Charisma checks when negotiating or bartering.

features.name: Street Network
features.description: You have a network of contacts throughout Neo-Tokyo that you can call upon for favors or information.

archetypes.name: Street Doc
archetypes.description: A skilled medic, patching up the wounded in back alleys and providing care outside the corporate system.

features.name: Field Medic
features.description: You can use your action to administer first aid to a wounded character, restoring 1d6 hit points.

features.name: Drug Synthesis
features.description: You can attempt to create basic medications and antidotes with a successful Intelligence (Medicine) check and the appropriate materials.

setting_skills.name: Streetwise
setting_skills.description: Knowledge of the urban underground and its inhabitants.

setting_skills.name: Hacking
setting_skills.description: Understanding of code and networks; used to gain access to and manipulate systems.
